pro_course_detail.title: Speak more like a native English speaker (Adults B1-C2) - Pronunciation, Common Expressions, Rhythm and more
pro_course_detail.description:
There are certain things that make it obvious that you're not a native English speaker. Pronunciation is only one small part of that.

In these sessions, I'll help you fully understand and improve all the areas that will help you speak more naturally like a native speaker.

We will cover:
- pronunciation (of course)
- common phrases, expressions & idioms (including what they mean, correct ways to say them, and appropriate times to use them + when not to use them)
- slang + which slang should not be used in a professional setting (you have to be careful with this)
- proper greetings + how to respond to different greetings
- appropriate greetings to use with your superiors vs. peers or subordinates (You want to be sure to get this right!)
- formal vs. informal language + appropriate times to use each one
- the correct rhythm of the English language + how it's different from your native language
- correct use of emphasis on words in a sentence to convey different meanings
- different ways to introduce yourself (or someone else) depending on if you're in person, on the phone, or via email
- correct use of prepositions, especially in/on/at (These can be confusing for non-native English speakers.)
- correct use of verb tenses (This is one of the biggest ways you can sound more natural right away.)
- how to properly pronounce letters when spelling words (and differences between British & American English)
- other differences between British & American English that you should know, especially depending on who you work with more often
- how to properly say numbers + how it's different depending on the type of number
- how to express units of measurement (like when to use things like carton, container, pack, package, etc.)
- and many more words, phrases, and ways to say things that will help you sound more natural when speaking

Having taught English for 14 years, I can quickly spot the areas you can improve to sound more natural. With my coaching, you will improve quickly.

pro_course_detail.title: IELTS Speaking
pro_course_detail.description:
In my IELTS Speaking classes, I’ll help you develop the skills and confidence necessary to excel in the exam and achieve your target score. We’ll work through authentic exam questions across all three parts, focusing on how to deliver well-structured, detailed responses, avoid common pitfalls, and naturally incorporate a range of vocabulary and grammar.

I’ll guide you on enhancing fluency, coherence, and response length, ensuring your answers are both articulate and confident. Each session is customized to your level and objectives, whether you're aiming for 6.5+ or need to improve from a 5.5. Through targeted practice and detailed feedback, you’ll gain clear strategies to elevate your performance.

pro_course_detail.title: IELTS Writing
pro_course_detail.description:
In my IELTS Writing classes, I’ll guide you in refining your writing skills to achieve a higher score on both Task 1 and Task 2. We will focus on crafting clear, concise, and well-organized essays, emphasizing effective question analysis, paragraph structure, and providing relevant examples to support your arguments.

I’ll help you develop strategies to improve task response, coherence, cohesion, lexical resource, and grammatical accuracy. Each lesson is tailored to your level and specific goals, whether you aim to elevate your score to Band 6.5 or progress further. You will receive comprehensive feedback and targeted guidance to enhance your writing style and overall performance.

pro_course_detail.title: Academic English
pro_course_detail.description:
In my Academic English classes, I focus on developing the key skills needed for success in university-level writing and communication. We will work on enhancing your academic writing, including essay structure, critical analysis, and the use of formal academic language. Special attention will be given to improving your ability to write clear, coherent arguments, conduct literature reviews, and cite sources correctly.

I’ll also help you master the nuances of academic vocabulary and grammar, ensuring you can express ideas precisely and effectively. Each lesson is personalized to address your specific academic goals, whether you’re preparing for university assignments or looking to improve your overall academic writing. You’ll receive constructive feedback and practical strategies to advance your writing proficiency and academic performance.

teacher_info.introduction:
I love conversation.  Through very natural and relaxed conversations, I'll offer up tips on pronunciation, American idioms, phrases, grammar, etc. You'll get practice with both speaking and listening, and will learn quite a few things about American English along the way.  I have an easy to understand North American accent, and am an easy-going person, who keeps conversations going easily and fluidly.  I'm interested in you, what you do, and what you think.  This curiosity drives the conversation, and forces you to push your limits with regards to English grammar and phraseology.
 
My background: I'm from the USA, from a city on the northeast coast called Boston. My original career, after university, was in video production.  I worked as a video editor. 
Over the last two years I have worked as an English teacher in Ecuador, Boston and Thailand. I taught conversational classes to students of all ages (children through adults), at an institute called Fine Tuned English.  I have taught all levels, from basic classes to advanced.  My advanced classes were based on the FCE exam--for which I helped my students prepare.  

Exam Preparation: I have experience in helping students practice for the IELTS and FCE (and a little bit with the TOEFL). I am familiar with the format of the tests, and with the grading criteria; however, I would not yet consider myself an expert. What I currently offer is practice with the oral section.  I'll ask you sample questions, and give you helpful suggestions on how to improve your answers, in relation to the tests' grading criteria. 

While I do have plenty of classroom experience, I feel that tutoring is much more effective for learning languages than are classrooms. teacher_info.about_me:
One of my greatest strengths as an accent coach, and as a person, is my ability to see the forest for the trees. ie, not get caught up in the less significant details. 
As your teacher, the first thing I'd do is diagnose which of your non-native sounds, speech patterns, or vocal settings, would improve your accent by a measure of 90%--if and when fixed. 
We'll then concentrate on addressing, practicing, and refining those specific elements of your accent. The other 10%, we can deal with secondarily.
teacher_info.about_teacher:

As a good accent coach and instructor, it's my job to comprehend and process all the little details that go into the vocal production of the American accent; and to provide you with what's most important for the improvement of your own accent. Presenting it all to you in an easily digestible way. 
That's essentially what I do.
teacher_info.teaching_style:
1) I'll listen to your pronunciation as we talk. Believe it or not, this is the BEST way to diagnose what's going on with your accent. If we want to fix your accent for use in real-life conversations, then we need to diagnose your accent issues, within a real conversation.  

2) We'll work together on the most glaring issues in your accent. If you can't make the sound, I'll help you to produce it. 

3) Once the sound is produceable, we'll use repetition of it within sentences, to get it into your muscle memory. Repetition is crucial for muscle memory retention. We'll also shadow (mimic) native speakers in series, movies and podcasts. I'll be giving you continual feedback as we progress.

pro_course_detail.title: American Pronunciation & Accent Coaching
pro_course_detail.description:
Learn how to speak with the North American accent.
Pronunciation is not only about individual sounds, it also involves intonation and Word Groups: Groups of words that flow together. This is a key aspect to North American pronunciation. We are a mumbling people. Our language is casual, and it flows. As a non-native, you're used to separating almost every word, using strong consonant sounds. In music theory that's called 'staccato'. But it's very un-American to speak that way. I will teach you how to modify sounds in order to create the American flow in your own speech.

You'll learn all about American speech patterns, intonation, tongue positioning, voice placement, breath, shadowing; stop consonants, vowel reductions, word linking, function/content words, the schwa, which sounds Americans erase--and when, the Flap T, pitch and syllable stress, voiced vs. unvoiced, and more.  

You can continue on with me as your accent coach, or take the self-practice I teach you, and improve on your own. But with the matrials and knowledge I provide, the choice will be yours.
